## Section 1: Domain Overview

`packages/water/` is the tank/borehole plumbing system — unrelated to this
package. `utilities/` is for consumable deliveries with their own stock/
order/cost lifecycle: bottled drinking water (Section 2-7) and LPG gas
bottles for the stove/heater (Section 8).

### Out of Scope (explicit)

| Topic | Owner |
|---|---|
| Tank/borehole water refill lifecycle | `packages/water/` |
| Water/tank safety aborts, audit trail | `packages/water/a_water_lifecycle_contract.yaml` |
| Prepaid electricity | `packages/power/prepaid_*.yaml` (the pattern this domain's cost tracking is modeled on) |

## Section 3: Stock Model

No sensor exists anywhere for bottle level (the dispenser reports nothing to
HA) — same situation as the vacuum's water/detergent tracker
(`packages/integrations/vacuum.yaml`), same fix: manual-log + self-
calibrating estimate.

- **`input_number.watercooler_bottles_in_stock`** — full **spare** bottles on
  hand, NOT counting the one currently mounted on the dispenser.
- **`sensor.watercooler_current_bottle_fraction_remaining`** — the mounted
  bottle's estimated remaining fraction (0–1), computed purely from elapsed
  time since `input_datetime.watercooler_last_bottle_change_time` against
  `input_number.watercooler_avg_days_per_bottle` — never a manual number.
- **`sensor.watercooler_bottles_remaining_total`** = stock + that fraction —
  the "how many bottles left" headline figure.
- **`sensor.watercooler_days_stock_remaining`** = total × avg days/bottle.
- The dispenser's own ~5L internal cooling reservoir
  (`input_number.watercooler_cooler_reservoir_liters`) is informational
  only — **not** counted in any of the above.
- Pressing **Log Bottle Changed** (`input_button.watercooler_log_bottle_
  changed`) is the only way any of this moves: EMA-refines the avg-days
  estimate (0.6 old / 0.4 new, same weighting as the vacuum's water-refill
  estimator), decrements spare stock by 1, increments empties-on-hand by 1,
  resets the elapsed-time clock.

## Section 4: Order → Delivery → Invoice Lifecycle

Three distinct, deliberately separate steps:

1. **Place Order** (`input_button.watercooler_place_order`) — records qty +
   timestamp, sets `input_boolean.watercooler_order_in_progress` on. The
   delivery-date picker (`input_datetime.watercooler_order_delivery_date`)
   is filled in by hand — `sensor.watercooler_next_delivery_options` shows
   the next few valid Mon/Wed/Fri dates (≥ `watercooler_order_lead_days`
   out) as **guidance only**, no hard gate, per explicit instruction ("no
   hard cutoff, generally 2 work days, tighter toward the weekend").
   `sensor.watercooler_suggested_order_qty` pre-suggests a seasonal qty
   (`watercooler_summer_order_qty`/`_winter_order_qty`, both editable) —
   caveat: the one real data point so far (delivered 6 Jul 2026, "winter" by
   this rule) was 8, not 7. Not silently resolved — flagged on the sensor's
   `note` attribute.
2. **Delivery Reminder** fires the morning of the chosen date
   (`watercooler_delivery_reminder_time`), only while an order is in
   progress and today matches the delivery date.
3. **Confirm Delivery** (`input_button.watercooler_confirm_delivery`) —
   `_delivery_confirmed_qty` bottles are added to stock,
   `_delivery_empties_taken` are subtracted from empties-on-hand, both feed
   the **live/physical** month counters (`_month_bottles_delivered`/
   `_month_empties_returned`, reset on the 1st) used only for
   `sensor.watercooler_net_deposit_exposure` — a mid-cycle estimate of what
   Aquazania's own deposit-invoice formula (delivered − returned, net
   shortfall only) will likely bill before the real invoice arrives. Closes
   `_order_in_progress` if one was open.

**Invoice logging is a separate, financial-record track — not the same data
as step 3.** The monthly ritual: paste the Aquazania invoice into a Claude
Code session (an `input_datetime.watercooler_invoice_reminder_time`/`_day`
nudge fires monthly, no button — the action is a chat session, not an HA
tap). Claude parses it and updates `watercooler_invoice_history.json`
directly (Bash/Edit, not an HA automation or pyscript service — see Section
5 for why). `sensor.watercooler_invoice_history` (a `command_line:` platform
sensor) surfaces the file's `summary` block into HA; `sensor.watercooler_
month_actual_cost`/`_year_actual_cost` filter its `monthly_breakdown`
attribute by the live calendar month/year — genuinely live, not stale
between edits.

---

## Section 5: Why the invoice history is a file, not a helper or pyscript

Two mechanisms were tried and rejected, both confirmed live against this HA
build (2026.8.3) before committing to the file-based design, not assumed:

1. **`input_text` holding a growing JSON array** — HA caps every entity's
   `state` string at 255 characters. Breaks after a handful of invoice
   records.
2. **A `pyscript` service writing a JSON file** — pyscript explicitly
   excludes `open()` from its builtins ("avoid i/o", see
   `custom_components/pyscript/eval.py`'s `BUILTIN_EXCLUDE`) regardless of
   `allow_all_imports`. No file I/O is possible from pyscript in this
   install. `recorder.import_statistics` (the core service that would
   otherwise be the sanctioned way to backfill dated statistics) is also not
   registered in this HA build's service list — checked live via the
   Supervisor API, not assumed from general HA knowledge.

**What actually works**: Claude Code sessions have normal filesystem access
outside any HA sandbox, so `watercooler_invoice_history.json` is maintained
directly (dedup-checked against `records[].reference` before every append),
and a `command_line:` sensor (`cat` the file, `json_attributes_path` into
`summary`) is the well-established core-HA pattern for surfacing an
externally-maintained JSON file as a sensor. This also matches the user's
actual stated workflow — paste the invoice into a session, not fill in a
dashboard form.

**Bulk backfill** (last year's invoices, flagged as coming in a later
session): same mechanism, called once per invoice, or the file hand-edited
directly for a batch import — the dedup check (`reference` field, plus an
identical date+total guard) applies either way.

## Section 6: Alert Pipeline

Canonical shape, copied structurally from `route_deebot_alert` /
`deebot_alert_cancel_from_notification` / `deebot_alert_snooze_reset`
(`packages/integrations/vacuum.yaml`):

```
binary_sensor.watercooler_low_stock
  (days_stock_remaining <= warning threshold, gated by watercooler_alert_notify)
        ↓
sensor.watercooler_alert_context  (warning / critical / normal)
        ↓
route_watercooler_alert  (script.notify_system_event, Cancel Alert button
                           both mobile + Telegram, immediate + 30min + 60min
                           repeat while unsnoozed)
        ↓
sensor.alert_device_entities  (aggregator — picked up automatically purely
                                by the `_alert_context` naming convention)
        ↓
sensor.global_alert_context  → dashboard + notification scripts
```

`alert.watercooler_alert` exists only for aggregator/dashboard visibility
and `can_acknowledge` UI — **not** the real delivery path (that's
`route_watercooler_alert`, same disclaimer as the vacuum's `alert:` block).
Requires a full HA restart to activate (`alert:` entities cannot be
reloaded).

## Section 7: Cost Model — VAT and rate constants

Confirmed against the actual Jul 2026 Aquazania invoice's own line math
(account J077431): every Unit Price/Net Price/Subtotal is **ex-VAT**; VAT
(exactly 15%) is added on top to reach the inclusive Total. So:

| Constant | Value (ex VAT) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `watercooler_water_price_per_bottle` | R72.00 | Invoice JAI3533243 |
| `watercooler_delivery_surcharge_per_bottle` | R3.20 | Invoice JAI3533243 |
| `watercooler_deposit_net_price_per_bottle` | R63.00 per **net** bottle not returned that month | Invoice JBI2164911 |
| `watercooler_vat_rate` | 15% | Verified: R90.24/R601.60 = R9.45/R63.00 = 0.15 |
| `watercooler_monthly_rental_reference` | R300 full rate | Invoice JRR2929107 — **reference only**, see below |

**Rental is not formula-derivable.** Aquazania bills a variable factor of
the full rate based on usage (Jul 2026: billed at 50% = R150, due to a
first-month-free proration — not a repeatable formula). `sensor.watercooler_
estimated_monthly_total_cost` uses the reference constant and is explicitly
flagged as an estimate; the real figure only ever comes from the invoice
history log (Section 4/5).

## Section 8: Gas Bottles

### 8a. Overview

2× 9kg LPG cylinders power the gas stove (year-round, main use) and a
movable gas heater (winter only). Unlike Water Cooler's anonymous bottle
stock, these are **two individually-identified cylinders with different
replenishment mechanics**:

- **Owned** — refillable, taken to a supplier and refilled.
- **Swap** — not owned, a full cylinder exchanged for the empty one at a
  supplier (never refilled).

Connection is manual (no dual-bottle auto-changeover regulator) — each
appliance has its own single-bottle hose, reconnected by hand. Both bottles
CAN be in use simultaneously (one per appliance) — confirmed live 2026-09-02:
Swap bottle on the stove, Owned bottle on the heater (near-empty from recent
use). **Main focus for most of the year is the stove** — the heater is only
connected in winter, and its estimate sensor reports full/idle whenever
nothing is assigned to it.

### 8b. File Inventory

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `packages/utilities/gas_helpers.yaml` | input_select (bottle identity per appliance, bottle status), input_number (burn-rate averages, price references, thresholds, reminder interval), input_datetime (per-appliance connected-since clocks, order/completion timestamps), input_boolean (do-refill/do-swap toggles, order-in-progress, EMA guards, alert notify/snooze), input_button (Place Order, Log Refill/Exchange Done) |
| `packages/utilities/gas_core.yaml` | `command_line:` sensor reading the gauge-photo history file + all template sensors (per-appliance stock estimate, order status, transaction log, actual cost, alert context) |
| `packages/utilities/gas_automations.yaml` | Bottle Reassigned (stove/heater) / Place Order / Order Reminder / Log Refill-Exchange Done / Gauge Reading Reminder / alert routing trio / `alert:` block |
| `packages/utilities/gas_gauge_history.json` | Claude-maintained photographed-gauge reading trend — see Section 8f |

Dashboard: Operations → **Gas Bottles** (`gas-control`), linked from a
Home-dashboard summary card next to Water Cooler's — same pattern as every
other domain. New skill: `.claude/commands/log-gas-reading.md` (mirrors
`/log-water-invoice`, see Section 8f).

### 8c. Stock Model — per-appliance, not per-bottle-pool

No sensor exists anywhere for gas remaining (same "no telemetry, manual-log +
self-calibrating estimate" situation as Water Cooler and the vacuum's water/
detergent tracker). The key departure from Water Cooler's model: consumption
is tracked **per appliance** (stove, heater), not per bottle-pool, because
each appliance's burn rate is very different and each can have a different
bottle connected:

- **`input_select.gas_stove_bottle_identity`** / **`gas_heater_bottle_
  identity`** — Owned / Swap / None — which physical bottle currently feeds
  which appliance. Heater defaults to `None` most of the year.
- **`input_datetime.gas_stove_bottle_connected_time`** / **`gas_heater_
  bottle_connected_time`** — since-when clock per appliance, reset whenever
  that appliance's identity select changes to a real bottle
  (`automation.gas_bottle_reassigned_stove`/`_heater`) OR whenever that
  bottle is refilled/exchanged in place without changing which appliance
  it's on (`automation.gas_confirm_completed` — see 8d).
- **`sensor.gas_stove_fraction_remaining`** / **`gas_heater_fraction_
  remaining`** — elapsed-time estimate against the matching avg-days
  input_number, same shape as `sensor.watercooler_current_bottle_fraction_
  remaining`. The heater one reports `1` (full/idle, never alertable)
  whenever its identity select is `None`.
- **`sensor.gas_stove_days_remaining`** / **`gas_heater_days_remaining`** =
  fraction × that appliance's avg-days input_number.
- **`input_number.gas_avg_days_per_bottle_stove`** (seed 75d) / **`gas_avg_
  days_per_bottle_heater`** (seed 21d) — pure seed guesses (user's own
  words: "2-3 months" stove-only, "2-4 weeks" with heater in proper winter;
  midpoints taken), EMA-refined (0.6 old / 0.4 new, same weighting used
  throughout this repo) by real elapsed time whenever either identity select
  changes OR a refill/exchange completes for whichever bottle is currently
  assigned to that appliance. **Flagged guesses, not measurements** — same
  caveat as the vacuum's manual-clean tracker seeds, don't cite 75/21 as
  real data until refined by actual presses.
- **`input_select.gas_owned_bottle_status`** / **`gas_swap_bottle_status`**
  — per-cylinder status (Ready/In Use/Empty/Out For Refill or Exchange),
  independent of which appliance it's on. User-editable, automation-assisted
  only at the specific "just completed" moment (see 8d) — not a full state
  machine, matching Water Cooler's light-touch-automation-on-top-of-manual-
  buttons philosophy.

### 8d. Order → Completion Lifecycle

Two entry points into the **same** completion action, unlike Water Cooler's
strict Place Order → Confirm Delivery sequence — most real trips today are
ad-hoc self-pickup with no advance order:

1. **Place Order** (`input_button.gas_place_order`, optional) — records
   order placed/expected date, sets `input_boolean.gas_order_in_progress`
   on. `automation.gas_order_reminder` nudges the morning of the expected
   date, same shape as Water Cooler's delivery reminder.
2. **Log Refill/Exchange Done** (`input_button.gas_confirm_completed`) — the
   real completion event, works whether or not step 1 happened. Reads
   `input_boolean.gas_do_refill` / `gas_do_swap` (either or both — a winter
   trip often does both at once, per the user's own stated pattern), and
   `input_number.gas_order_refill_cost` / `gas_order_swap_cost`. For each
   service that happened: marks that bottle's status Ready (Full); if that
   bottle is the one currently assigned to an appliance, EMA-updates that
   appliance's avg-days and resets its connected-since clock (the "same
   bottle refilled in place" case that a bare identity-select change would
   never catch, since the select value doesn't change). Records
   `input_datetime.gas_last_completed_time`, clears `gas_order_in_progress`
   if one was open, resets the do-refill/do-swap toggles and cost fields
   back to idle, and fires a `gas_transaction_logged` event (see 8e).

### 8e. Transaction Log — cost/usage tracking without a JSON file

Unlike Water Cooler's invoice history (a Claude-maintained file, needed
because invoices are pasted documents), gas transactions are entirely
dashboard-button-driven, so `sensor.gas_transaction_log` is a **self-
referencing trigger-based template sensor** instead — the CODING_STANDARDS
"time-series without a recorder query" pattern
(`sensor.device_battery_history_log`-style, `alerts_device_batteries.yaml`).
It appends one row (`date`, `refill`, `swap`, `refill_cost`, `swap_cost`,
`stove_bottle`, `heater_bottle`) per completed transaction, capped to a
rolling 120 entries, entirely HA-native — no Claude session needed to write
to it. `sensor.gas_month_actual_cost` / `gas_year_actual_cost` filter its
`log` attribute by the live calendar month/year.

**Design note — event-triggered, not button-state-triggered**: the sensor
triggers off a custom `gas_transaction_logged` event fired by
`automation.gas_confirm_completed`, not off `input_button.gas_confirm_
completed`'s own state change directly. That automation captures the do-
refill/do-swap/cost values into variables, then later in the same run resets
those same helpers back to idle — if the sensor instead read those helpers
live off the button's state-change trigger, it would race the automation's
own reset with no ordering guarantee between an automation and a trigger-
based template entity reacting to the same trigger. The event carries an
immutable snapshot as `event_data`, so there's nothing to race. Confirmed
live 2026-09-02: also hit two config-shape errors building this — a trigger-
based sensor must be its own list item under `template:` (not nested inside
a plain `sensor:` list, and not a second top-level `template:` key in the
same file — both rejected/silently-broken, see `gas_core.yaml`'s inline
comments) — and Jinja dict `.update()` is blocked by HA's template sandbox
(`SecurityError: access to attribute 'update' of 'dict' object is unsafe`);
the dashboard's monthly aggregation charts use the same `dict(list_of_
tuples)` fold `sensor.device_battery_history_log` already used for exactly
this reason, not a mutated dict.

### 8f. Gauge Reading History — separate from cost/usage tracking

The stove has a manual gauge (no equivalent exists for the heater).
`packages/utilities/gas_gauge_history.json` is a small, Claude-maintained
file (same file-not-helper reasoning as `watercooler_invoice_history.json`,
Section 5) logging photographed gauge readings via the new `/log-gas-
reading` skill, on a reminder cycle (`automation.gas_gauge_reading_
reminder`, interval `input_number.gas_gauge_reminder_interval_days` — starts
at 14, user's stated plan is to move to 30 once the trend is established).
`sensor.gas_gauge_history` (a `command_line:` sensor) surfaces it, same
pattern as `sensor.watercooler_invoice_history`.

**Deliberately NOT fed into the avg-days EMAs** (8c) — this is a trend/
calibration reference only, shown on the dashboard, same "informational
only, not counted" precedent as Water Cooler's dispenser reservoir. The
EMAs only update from real refill/exchange completions (8d/8e).

**⚠️ Open as of 2026-09-02**: no photo of the actual gauge has successfully
been read in a session yet (upload attempts failed client-side, not a code
issue). The exact reading format (kg scale, %, or colour-zone) is therefore
unconfirmed — `/log-gas-reading`'s own file flags this and must be updated
with the real format the first time a photo is successfully parsed, rather
than guessing now.

### 8g. Alert Pipeline

Exact structural copy of Water Cooler's (Section 6), `route_gas_alert` /
`gas_alert_cancel_from_notification` / `gas_alert_snooze_reset` /
`alert.gas_alert`. `binary_sensor.gas_low` fires when either appliance's
days-remaining is at/under `input_number.gas_warning_days_remaining`, gated
by `input_boolean.gas_alert_notify` — the heater side is only ever
considered while a bottle is actually assigned to it (identity ≠ `None`).
Requires a full HA restart to activate (`alert:` entities cannot be
reloaded) — same disclaimer as every other domain's `alert:` block.

### 8h. Cost Model — price references

Unlike Water Cooler's invoice-derived, VAT-verified constants, gas pricing
is **rough reference only**, refined by real logged transaction costs rather
than a parsed-invoice pipeline (user's explicit call — self-pickup pricing
varies by supplier and delivery is untested):

| Constant | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `gas_owned_refill_price_reference` | R330 | Gas Affair, self-pickup (cheaper option) |
| `gas_swap_exchange_price_reference` | R309 | Gas Affair, self-pickup |

BigF Gas Randburg quoted ~R390 (more expensive) but which service that
figure covers (refill vs. exchange) is unconfirmed, so it isn't seeded as a
constant — noted here rather than guessed into the YAML. Gas Affair's
combo price for both together was ~R639. Delivery pricing from either
supplier has not been tried.
